summary:
Jüri Reinvere (born 1971) is an Estonian composer, poet and essayist whose music and writing explore history, politics, nature and human perception. He received the 2025 OPUS Klassik award for Composer of the Year.

Raised in Tallinn, he studied composition in Warsaw and Helsinki, then moved to Germany in 2005. He has lived in Frankfurt since 2017. His work combines modernist sound with romantic elements and often joins contemporary techniques to classical forms and narratives.

Reinvere has written orchestral, choral and chamber music, poetry-based works, and operas. His operas include *Puhdistus*, premiered in Helsinki in 2012; *Peer Gynt*, premiered in Oslo in 2014; and *Minona*, premiered in Regensburg. His oratorio *The Expulsion of Ishmael* was premiered in Berlin in 2022.

He also writes about cultural and political affairs for Estonian and German newspapers. His journalism has earned several awards, including Estonia’s Ethical Essayists Award in 2017 and the Jaan Tõnisson Prize in 2023.
